comments.note: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Library/DapperMovieRepository.cs: The original comment '// movies_filenames does not store an insertion timestamp; return any match.' was stale (added before the created_at column existed). Removed it as part of this WP since the ORDER BY now makes the behaviour deterministic.

src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Database/migrations/m039_add_filenames_created_at.sql: The legacy UNIQUE KEY `hash_2 (hash)` on `movies_filenames` prevented multiple filenames per movie, which contradicts the intended design (same video at multiple paths is valid). This constraint was inherited from the legacy app's migration (spdb-indexer DBHelper.cs line 851). Removing it in m039 restores the intended behaviour but was not originally in the WP scope — it was a necessary prerequisite for the AC-6 integration test to be meaningful.

tests/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests/Library/DapperMovieRepositoryTests.cs: The GetOriginalFilenameAsync_WithMultipleFilenames_ReturnsEarliest test uses a hardcoded DateTime(2000, 1, 1) for the 'earlier' timestamp. This is reliable since CURRENT_TIMESTAMP in the 'later' row will always be decades ahead of year 2000.

src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/Database/migrations/: Migration files lack a naming convention document. The pattern is `m{revision}_{description}.sql` with lowercase snake_case descriptions — this is consistent across m036–m039 but not documented in constraints.md or the manifest.
